title: induction-tab
gist: Open a tab and a small transformer trains from nothing on your own GPU until it learns to copy what it has just seen, the transition known as induction. It runs in hand-written WGSL with nothing to install, and afterward you can type at the model and silence the heads doing the copying.
summary: Lets you watch induction heads form in a small transformer in your own browser, then type at the model and silence its heads, with nothing to install.

hero_image.alt: The live page after a finished run. A random row of characters sits above its exact repeat, lit in blue where the model predicts it. A typed hello hello hello prompt carries on by itself, two layer 0 heads and all four layer 1 heads draw a sharp line in their attention maps, and a chart shows copy advantage rising past the 2-nat event.

site.eyebrow: Hand-written WGSL trainer · study arms of up to 64 seeds · MIT
site.blurb: A small transformer trains through the induction transition in a browser tab, on your own GPU, in hand-written WGSL, and then you can type at it and silence its heads. In a seeds study on a smaller model, the repeat rule was the largest single-factor contrast I could bound in steps, and tying weights delayed the event at depths 2 to 4 at both learning rates I tested. A rescaled threshold I preregistered failed on one arm, 0.903 against 0.901.
site.paper_title: Induction heads in a browser tab: a hand-written WebGPU trainer, and what the repeat rule and weight tying do to onset
